sections.html:
Craven County Tax Administration, at 226 Pollock Street in New Bern, both appraises real estate and collects the bills. Weekday counter hours are eight to five. Call the real estate appraisal division at 252-636-6640 with value questions, and the tax collection division at 252-636-6605 about bills.

Business personal property and non-business personal property each have their own division. Vehicles are taxed through the state's tag-and-tax system, which a house seller can generally skip unless a closing statement lists a vehicle gap bill.

Eight municipalities sit in the county: Bridgeton, Cove City, Dover, Havelock, New Bern, River Bend, Trent Woods and Vanceboro. About 105,025 people live here, in 50,334 housing units. Owners live in 68.4% of homes, and the typical owner-occupied house was worth $231,600 in 2020 to 2024.

The commissioners kept the 2026-2027 county rate at 44.48 cents per $100 of assessed value. This is only the county levy. A town or district charge may sit on top, and the 2026 tax rates document on the county site shows it.

The rate applies to assessed value after any exclusion you hold. Three state programs exist.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: $25,000 or 50% of a permanent residence's appraised value, whichever is greater, is removed from taxation, provided income is within $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 of appraised value is excluded. Age and income do not matter.
  • Circuit breaker: your bill is capped at 4.0% of income, or 5.0% when income exceeds the limit but stays within 150% of it, which is $58,200 for 2026.

Apply on Form AV-9 with the assessor. Applications are taken until June 1 of the preceding year, and each program has its own page on the county tax menu.

Value and rate are separate decisions. Revaluation fixes market value; the commissioners fix the rate to cover the budget. So a higher assessment is not itself a higher rate, though an unchanged rate still yields a bigger bill if your value rises.

Billing opens September 1, and interest-free payment ends January 5. The collection calendar runs like this.

Craven County tax collection calendar
DateWhat happens
September 1Bills are due (state law)
January 5Final interest-free day
January 6Taxes are delinquent
Mid-JanuaryDelinquent tax notices mailed
Mid-FebruaryDebt setoff notices mailed, and attachment and garnishment proceed
March 31Final day to pay and stay off the published delinquent list

Under G.S. 105-360, interest opens at 2% on January 6 and climbs three-fourths of one percent for every month or fraction beginning February 1.

• Online at my.cravencountync.gov. A name, address or parcel number finds the bill, and scheduled or partial payments are possible.
  • By mail to Craven County Tax Collector, PO Box 1128, New Bern, NC 28563-1128.
  • In person at 226 Pollock Street by check, cash, money order or card, or through the drop box at the building's front right. Keep cash out of the drop box.

The tax menu also lists pre-payments and a delinquent payment assistance page. For delinquent bills, the county refers owners to NCHomeownerAssistance.gov and the state hotline 1-855-696-2423.

Ahead of a sale, get a payoff figure covering the current year and any earlier unpaid ones. The real property tax lien attaches as of the listing date (G.S. 105-355), so a payoff letter protects buyer and seller alike.

Tax year 2023 carried the most recent revaluation, and tax year 2028 is next. The 2028 values will be market value as of January 1 of that year. A Revaluation 2028 page is already online, with a comparable-sales search tool marked "coming February 2028."

Under G.S. 105-286 no more than eight years may separate revaluations, and a county of 75,000 or more can be required to revalue sooner if sales assessment ratios fall below .85 or rise above 1.15. Craven has run a shorter cycle than the statute requires, and Hurricane Florence in 2018 pushed the planned 2020 revaluation to 2023.

If you sell before 2028, your parcel's value will date from that 2023 revaluation.

Send a signed appeal form to the county assessor before the date printed on your value notice, which in a revaluation year is the board's adjournment date.

  • Include comparable sales from on or before January 1 of the revaluation year, photos showing the property's condition, and any recent appraisal or market analysis.
  • The owner, an attorney or an agent under power of attorney can sign. A close family member may also appear when the owner cannot, such as during unexpected military duty or a hospital stay.
  • An appraiser reviews the file and mails a result: higher, lower or unchanged.
  • Still in disagreement? The Board of Equalization and Review hears the case and sends a hearing letter at least 15 days ahead.
  • Bring a copy of your evidence for each of the seven board members.

After the board comes the Property Tax Commission. File written notice within 30 days of the date the board mails its decision, with a copy to the assessor (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: Other tax pages that may affect a listing
sections.html:
Several pages on the county tax menu can change a bill or a listing:

  • A Present Use Value Exclusion page.
  • Historic Properties, Builders Exclusion, Religious Uses Exemption and Antique Airplane and Automobile Exclusion pages.
  • A gross receipts rental tax report and an occupancy and tourism development tax form, which matter to anyone selling a rental.
  • Change of mailing address forms, so a seller's final bill reaches the right place after closing.

sections.h2: What to ask before you list
sections.html:
A few calls early on save trouble later. Ask the appraisal division at 252-636-6640 how your parcel was valued in 2023 and when the next revaluation will arrive. Ask tax collection at 252-636-6605 whether anything is open from an earlier year. If you rent the property, ask whether the gross receipts rental tax report or the occupancy and tourism development tax form still needs filing. Finally, file a change of mailing address so your last bill finds you.

Having those answers in hand makes the payoff figure and the settlement statement easy to check.

Request from tax collection a payoff covering every unpaid year, then give it to the closing attorney so it comes out of your proceeds. A delinquent bill follows the calendar above: notices in January, setoff and garnishment in February, and a published list after March 31.

When repairs or back taxes stand in the way of an ordinary sale, our North Carolina page explains a cash route. Whichever way you sell, the lien is settled at closing.

faqs.q: When are Craven County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are due September 1, and January 5 is the last interest-free day. Delinquency starts January 6, when 2% interest begins.

faqs.q: What is the Craven County property tax rate?
faqs.a: For fiscal year 2026-2027 the county rate stayed at 44.48 cents per $100. The 2026 tax rates document shows any town or district charge.

faqs.q: When is the next Craven County revaluation?
faqs.a: Tax year 2028. The last one took effect in 2023.

faqs.q: Who can appeal a Craven County valuation?
faqs.a: Owners, attorneys and agents holding power of attorney may sign. File comparable sales, photos or an appraisal with the county assessor by the date on your notice.

faqs.q: What follows if a Craven County bill is unpaid after January 5?
faqs.a: Delinquency begins January 6. Notices follow in mid-January, setoff notices and garnishment steps in mid-February, and a newspaper list appears after March 31.
